key_insight: SymAnt combines neural prediction with adaptable symbolic priors to anticipate long sequences of human actions from brief observations. Its central idea is to pair flexible learned representations with structured reasoning.
problem_solved: Anticipating many future actions from limited observations is difficult, while purely neural approaches can require extensive input and be hard to interpret or adjust.
method: Use a neuro-symbolic approach to combine neural networks with structured symbolic reasoning.
Ground long-horizon action anticipation in adaptable symbolic priors.
Note: The supplied abstract is incomplete, so implementation details and evaluation results are unavailable.
impact: SymAnt offers a direction toward action anticipation that is easier to interpret and adapt, potentially supporting robots and other human-interactive systems. The provided excerpt does not establish measured performance gains.
visual_elements: Timeline showing a brief observed action sequence followed by a longer anticipated sequence.
Two-branch diagram merging neural representations and symbolic priors into future-action predictions.
Illustrative symbolic graph connecting a scene, objects, and possible actions.
Editable-prior icon showing how changing a symbolic rule could influence anticipated actions.
paper_title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
paper_authors: Fnu Aryan, Yaqi Xie, Joseph Campbell, Woojun Kim, Kwonjoon Lee
